record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Fix an odd socle degree j. Let F be a general degree-j form in n variables, with n >= 6 or (n, j) = (5, >= 5) or (n, j) = (4, >= 15), excluding (7, 3), and let Γ = Spec(S/Ann(F)) ⊆ A^n. Is the degree-<0 part of the tangent space at [Γ] equal to n?

evidence.quote: Problem XVIII (General forms of odd degree [73, Conjecture 6.30]). Fix an odd j. Let F be a general form of degree j in n variables ... Let Γ = Spec(S/ Ann(F)) ⊆ A^n. Is it true that dim(T[Γ])<0 = n?

artifact.category_tag: Hilbert schemes of points and Gorenstein algebras
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture (regarding the negative-degree part of the tangent space at the punctual Gorenstein scheme cut out by a general odd-degree form) in the list of open problems on deformations of Artinian algebras and Hilbert schemes. Web searches turn up related work on compressed Gorenstein algebras and elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme, but no source resolving this specific equality $\dim (T_{[\Gamma]})_{<0}=n$ for general odd-degree forms in the listed ranges. No proof or counterexample was located.

status_evidence.title: New elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tangent spaces and trivial negative tangents at points of the Hilbert scheme corresponding to apolar algebras of general forms, but does not resolve the equality in the stated ranges.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on tangent spaces at Gorenstein points of Hilb does not establish the conjectured equality.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2504.07541 (compressed Gorenstein / generic forms)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Ann(F) for generic forms F and compressed Gorenstein algebras but does not state a resolution of the negative-degree tangent space conjecture in the indicated ranges.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on apolar ideals of general odd-degree forms does not confirm a solution.
